questions: Should the one-hot encoding be based on the distinct elements across the entire merged list, or should it treat each sublist separately?
What should be the order of categories in the one-hot encoding? For example, sorted order, order of first appearance, or something else?
Are the elements within the sublists guaranteed to be hashable and comparable (e.g., integers, strings) to allow distinct identification?
Should the output array have dtype integer or float?
Is the function expected to handle empty sublists or an empty list of lists?
Should the one-hot encoding produce a dense array (as in the reference) or a sparse matrix?
Are duplicate elements within a sublist or across sublists intended to be encoded as separate instances or as the same category?
What should be the shape of the output? Should it be (n_samples, n_categories) as in the reference, or could it be transposed?
